item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 241742
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Sat Oct 24 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Vance, located several hundred miles southwest of Acapulco, Mexico.

Western Central Pacific:
Shower activity associated with a broad area of low pressure located
near or just west of the International Date Line, several hundred
miles west of Johnston Atoll, has become a little better organized
since yesterday. Environmental conditions could support some
continued slow development while the system crosses the Dateline and
moves generally eastward to east-northeastward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...20 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

$$
Forecaster Beven

item.title: Hurricane Vance Public Advisory Number 14
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM CST Sat Oct 24 2026 
000
WTPZ32 KNHC 242039
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Vance Advisory Number  14
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
300 PM CST Sat Oct 24 2026
 
...VANCE WEAKENS SOME MORE AS IT CONTINUES NORTH-NORTHWESTWARD...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 300 PM CST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...13.3N 103.3W
ABOUT 335 MI...540 KM SW OF ACAPULCO MEXICO
ABOUT 400 MI...640 KM S OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...90 MPH...150 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NNW OR 340 DEGREES AT 6 MPH...9 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...977 MB...28.85 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests along the southwestern coast of Mexico should monitor the
progress of Vance. A Tropical Storm Watch may be required for
portions of the southwestern coast of Mexico tonight or on Sunday.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 300 PM CST (2100 UTC), the center of Hurricane Vance was located
near latitude 13.3 North, longitude 103.3 West. Vance is moving
toward the north-northwest near 6 mph (9 km/h), and a slow motion
toward the north-northwest is expected to continue through Monday.
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 90 mph (150 km/h) 
with higher gusts.  Additional weakening is expected through Sunday 
night. Some re-intensification is possible on Monday.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 30 miles (45 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 150 miles
(240 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 977 mb (28.85 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
RAINFALL: Through next Thursday, Vance is expected to produce 4 to 6
inches with isolated higher totals around 10 inches across Colima
and western portions of Michoacán and Jalisco. This rainfall may
produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas
along steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Vance,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?rainqpf.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Vance will affect portions of the coast
of southern and southwestern Mexico this weekend and continue into
next week. These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf
and rip current conditions. Please consult products from your local
weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 900 PM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Beven

item.title: Hurricane Vance Forecast Discussion Number 14
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM CST Sat Oct 24 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 242040
TCDEP2
 
Hurricane Vance Discussion Number  14
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
300 PM CST Sat Oct 24 2026

Vance has become significantly less organized since the last 
advisory due to a combination of cold water near the center and 
increasing southwesterly shear. Microwave data indicates that the 
eyewall has broken open, with the remaining convection limited to 
north of the center. In addition, visible imagery shows the 
low-level center to be near or a little south of the southern edge 
of the convective mass. The various satellite intensity estimates 
have dropped, and based on them the initial intensity is lowered to 
80 kt.  This could be quite generous, as the current structure does 
not look much like a hurricane.
 
The intensity forecast is still problematic, but perhaps a little 
less so than earlier. Vance is likely to weaken during the next 
12-18 h as it crosses a pool of colder water with temperatures near 
27C that has been upwelled by several previous tropical cyclones, 
while at the same time it experiences at least moderate 
southwesterly shear.  Beyond that time, the center is expected to 
move over sea surface temperatures near 29C closer to the coast of 
Mexico. This could allow intensification if the shear is light 
enough and the storm structure is still good enough to allow it. The 
GFS and ECMWF continue show a period of reduced, but still marginal, 
shear that could allow some intensification, and based on this and 
trends in the guidance slight re-intensification is shown at 48 h. 
By the end of the forecast period, increasing shear is likely to 
cause Vance to steadily weaken. It is still possible that Vance 
could weaken more than forecast before reaching warmer water and 
that the shear may be too strong to allow re-intensification after 
36 h. The new intensity forecast has major downward adjustments from 
the previous forecast.

The initial motion remains north-northwestward or 340/5 kt.  Vance 
is being steered by a weak low- to mid-level ridge over eastern 
Mexico, and it is approaching a large mid-latitude trough over the 
western United States and northwestern Mexico. While neither of 
these features will change much during the next few days, Vance is 
likely to move into an area of lighter steering currents near the 
base of the trough and slow its forward motion during the next 
24 or so.  The track forecast beyond that time is dependent on the 
cyclone's strength and vertical structure. A weaker system that 
shears apart like shown in the UKMET and Canadian is likely to move 
west-northwestward to northwestward before resuming a more northerly 
motion, while a stronger and vertically deeper system is likely to 
continue slowly northward or north-northwestward.  The track 
guidance envelope has shifted westward since the previous advisory, 
and the new forecast track has been nudged westward as well. 
Additional westward adjustments to the track may be necessary if 
Vance continues to lose organization.


Key Messages:
 
1. Due to the uncertainties in both the track and intensity
forecasts, it is too early to say what wind and storm surge
impacts Vance may cause along the coast of Mexico. Interests in
southwestern Mexico should continue to monitor the progress of the
hurricane.
 
2. Heavy rainfall associated with slow-moving Hurricane Vance will 
impact the western coast of Mexico from Michoacán to Jalisco during 
much of next week. This rainfall may produce life-threatening 
flooding and mudslides across Colima and western portions of 
Michoacán and Jalisco, especially in areas along steep terrain.
